extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for the ERC Consolidator Grant (principal investigators ~7–12 years post-PhD)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and procedural guidance for applicants to the ERC Consolidator Grant, including the sole evaluation criterion of 'Excellence' (research project and PI), eligibility window, two-step panel review, and the 2026 change on feasibility assessment. Useful for preparing Part I (B1) and Part II (B2) of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence (sole evaluation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consolidator Grant is evaluated on the sole criterion of Excellence, which includes both the excellence of the research project and the excellence of the principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessment is framed under 'Excellence' — applicants must demonstrate excellence in both the proposed research and the PI. The panels primarily evaluate the ground‑breaking nature and ambition of the project, while also evaluating the intellectual capacity and creativity of the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research project — Ground‑breaking nature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly listed as a component of the research project's excellence; panels primarily evaluate the ground‑breaking nature of the project. Emphasize novelty, transformational potential, and the extent to which the project opens new directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research project — Ambition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition is a core element of the project assessment and is one of the primary foci of panels. Proposals should demonstrate high-risk/high-gain, ambitious objectives and scope appropriate for ERC funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Intellectual capacity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as part of PI excellence; panels assess the PI's intellectual strengths and ability to conceive major advances. Panels particularly evaluate intellectual capacity alongside creativity, with attention to the PI's scientific expertise and capacity to execute the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Creativity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creativity is assessed for the PI as a component of excellence. Demonstrate original thinking, novel approaches, and ability to drive innovative research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Commitment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment is part of the PI assessment. Applicants must show sufficient dedication/availability and a realistic commitment to carrying out the project successfully (e.g., time allocation, institutional support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Required scientific expertise and capacity to execute project
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the extent to which the PI has the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels evaluate whether the PI has the necessary track record, skills, leadership, and resources (including team and institutional environment) to deliver the proposed research. This is highlighted as a particular focus when assessing PI excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: PI must be 7-12 years post-PhD (with extensions for eligible career breaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an eligibility requirement for applicants to the Consolidator Grant; applicants must ensure they fall within this post-PhD time window or correctly apply permitted extensions for career breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review process — Two‑step evaluation (Step 1: B1 only; Step 2: B1 & B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-step evaluation: Step 1: A panel of generalist reviewers reads only B1. Step 2: If selected, the proposal moves to Step 2, where a new panel of specialists reviews both B1 and B2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare B1 (Part I) to stand alone for Step 1 assessment by generalists; if shortlisted, expect specialist review of both B1 and B2 at Step 2. The change in emphasis on what is assessed at each step should inform what content you include in each part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent external experts and access to materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels may be assisted by independent external experts working remotely, recommended by panel members collectively, with access to Part I, Part II, and the proposed budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External experts can be consulted and will see the submitted materials (Part I, Part II, budget). Applicants should assume expert scrutiny of scientific content and budget justification at the specialist review stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part I (B1) content guidance — Feasibility not to be included at Step 1 (2026 key change)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2026 Key Change: Feasibility will no longer be assessed at Step 1; thus, Part I of the Scientific Proposal should no longer include details on the feasibility of the scientific approach but present a convincing overall research strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include detailed feasibility arguments or methodological minutiae in Part I/B1 intended for Step 1 generalist reviewers. Instead, craft Part I to present a clear, convincing overall research strategy, emphasizing ground‑breaking nature and ambition; reserve detailed feasibility, methods, and implementation specifics for Part II/B2 where specialists will assess them.
